title: Round 768 (F1074): 14-byte cell record 100% CLOSED (14/14 bytes mapped) - F1073 note CORRECTED: bytes 12-13 ARE the attr word @+0xC already anchored by F1065 (0x43CA40 reads word[+0xC]; there is no separate 'attr dword high word'), so after F1065 (byte0, word@3, word@5, word@7, word@0xC), F1069 (blend bytes 1-2), F1072 (bytes 9, 11) and F1073 (byte10) the record is fully mapped: byte0 bit0 blocked; byte1 front-blend (hi&7*16+lo anim offset, bit7 float path); byte2 mid-blend; byte3 front file; byte4 mid file; bytes5-6 mid frame; bytes7-8 front frame; byte9 static id (cluster {9,10,11,58,60,61}) + rare bit7 (282 cells); byte10 static flag (0/0x04); byte11 runtime mark bit7; bytes12-13 attr word (bits14-15 file idx 0-3, nibble>>4 decal class, low nibble) - EMPIRICAL attr-word measurement over 3,352,976 cells (60 maps): nonzero on only 447 cells (0.013%, super-sparse decal/detail cells); file-idx distribution {0:235, 1:30, 2:12, 3:170} (all four sprite-file slots used); nibble>>4 in {0:31, 1:229, 2:10, 3:177} - ALL < 0xA, consistent with the render driver gate (0x41C4F6 cmp 0xA jge skip); low nibble in {0:58, 1:389}; decal tables mapobj+0xF5390 (1B) / +0xF5394 (3B) indexed by nibble feed 0x434A20
objective: Close the cell-record byte map and validate the attr word on real data.
question: Is any cell-record byte still unmapped, and how sparse is the attr word in real maps?
method: Cross-check F1065/F1069/F1072/F1073 field lists against the 14-byte layout; histogram word@0xC over 3.35M cells.
scope: full cell record; attr word consumers (0x43CA40, 0x41C460 driver).

final_layout.1: front blend (hi&7*16+lo -> anim table @+0x1B01D4; bit7 float)
final_layout.12-13: attr word: bits14-15 file idx, nibble>>4 decal class 0-9, low nibble

audit_vs_exe.F1073: note CORRECTED: bytes 12-13 = attr word (mapped since F1065), not an open field
